newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Two Americans missing in Cambodia light plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Two Americans missing in Cambodia light plane crash.

text.p: Two U.S. citizens were missing and feared dead after pieces of their light aircraft were spotted on Cambodia's highest mountain on Wednesday, a top American diplomat said.

"People on board (the rescue aircraft) said it didn't look good," the diplomat told Reuters, adding that the single- engined plane had gone down in heavy jungle on Mount Oral, some 90 km (55 miles) northwest of the capital Phnom Penh.

The men were said to have been taking part in a nighttime geological survey of the Tonle Sap lake basin for the Japan National Oil Corporation, which is exploring the likelihood of oil and gas reserves under Cambodia's vast inland lake.
The diplomat said there were two U.S. nationals on board, the pilot and a technician. He said they worked for the LCT Company of Houston, Texas, but would not give their names.
The government started searching for the plane when they realised it was overdue, and parts of the fuselage was spotted late on Wednesday.
